section_title: Can the God who rules everything overlook His weary people?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 9 Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news. Raise your voice loudly, O Jerusalem, herald of good news. Lift it up, do not be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!” 10 Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule. His reward is with Him, and His recompense accompanies Him. 11 He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.

12 Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand? Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance? 13 Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor? 14 Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice? Who imparted knowledge to Him and showed Him the way of understanding? 15 Surely the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are considered a speck of dust on the scales; He lifts up the islands like fine dust. 16 Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering. 17 All the nations are as nothing before Him; He regards them as nothingness and emptiness.

18 To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him? 19 To an idol that a craftsman casts and a metalworker overlays with gold and fits with silver chains? 20 One lacking such an offering chooses wood that will not rot. He seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.

21 Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the foundation of the earth? 22 He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth; its dwellers are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in. 23 He brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless. 24 No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground, than He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble. 25 “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One. 26 Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these? He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name. Because of His great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.

27 Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”? 28 Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out. 29 He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak. 30 Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall. 31 But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.

context_lines: Zion and Jerusalem are called to announce good news to Judah’s cities: their God is coming. His strength is joined to a shepherd’s care. He gathers lambs close to His heart and gently leads the nursing ewes.

The questions that follow make His greatness plain. Who measures the waters and heavens? Who weighs mountains or teaches the Lord justice? Nations are like a drop or a speck beside Him. Even Lebanon’s resources could not provide an offering equal to His greatness.

The comparison with idols exposes the absurdity of treating a crafted object as His equal. An idol must be made, decorated and secured so it will not fall. The Lord reigns above the earth, brings rulers low and calls the stars by name.

This reaches a very personal complaint: Israel feels its way is hidden and its claim ignored. The answer joins power with care. The everlasting Creator neither tires nor lacks understanding; He gives strength to the faint, and those who wait upon Him receive renewed strength.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/isaiah/40.htm) and [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/isaiah/40.htm) read the questions about creation and rule as grounds for trusting the comfort already announced. God does not need advice, assistance or an image made by human hands in order to act.

For the coming Lord in verse 10, [Gill](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/40.htm) discusses a reading focused on Christ’s second coming, but prefers His first coming in this context because of John’s preparation and the shepherd picture. Henry also connects the shepherd’s tenderness with Christ’s care for His people.

For the final complaint, Wesley and Gill understand hiddenness as the people’s feeling that their suffering and cause are being neglected. The answer is not that their pain is too small to matter, but that the Lord has the understanding and strength to sustain them.

Gill explains waiting as continuing in confidence, prayer and reliance on God, rather than simply standing still. The renewed strength is applied to persevering in faith and obedience through difficulty.
god_plan_lines: Paul directly uses Isaiah’s question about the Lord’s counselor in [Romans 11:33–36](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/11.htm). It concludes his discussion of God’s mercy to Jews and Gentiles with worship: the wisdom behind His purpose exceeds human ability to trace it.

In [1 Corinthians 2:9–16](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/2.htm), Paul again uses the question about knowing or instructing the Lord. He explains that God reveals His gifts through the Spirit and brings the discussion to the mind of Christ. The God who cannot be taught is the One who graciously makes His truth known.

The shepherd picture also has a clear parallel in [John 10:11–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/john/10.htm). Jesus describes His care through laying down His life for the sheep and gathering them into one flock. Together these connections show divine greatness serving a saving purpose: God reveals, gathers and sustains His people.
